subsection.title: dx as an oriented step
subsection.p: The definite integral
accumulates from a to b. The direction matters.
If a\lt b, we move left to right. A small step dx is positive.
If b\lt a, we move right to left. A small step dx is negative.
That is why
The symbol dx carries the direction of traversal.

That negative value is not a negative physical mass. It is the oriented accumulation from 4 back to 1. For physical mass, we choose the natural left-to-right orientation or take ordinary length.

paragraphs.title: Moral
paragraphs.p: The definite integral records both size and direction. Applications decide whether that signed quantity is the desired physical quantity.
